$comment: Mission 1.84. One machine-readable schema and one deterministic gate, both frozen before execution. Lexical filtering does not prove semantic safety and this contract does not claim it does: what it cannot name is why the execution stops for a human.

field_mapping.$comment: the mission brief's field names against the repository vocabulary that already carries them

numeric_confidence_note: a self-reported certainty is not a probability, so the field is a closed enum of one rather than a number. No score is requested, computed or persisted anywhere
failure_policy: a failure at any stage persists no Opportunity. The output is never repaired by a second model call, and a refusal is recorded rather than retried

two_stale_checks_generalised.$comment: found while building this contract, and both would have refused a truthful answer
two_stale_checks_generalised.reliability_assertion: the gate required the output to preserve NON_SCORABLE / MISSING_RELIABILITY. Every row in the corpus was non-scorable when Mission 1.31 wrote it; Mission 1.77 resolved reliability from lineage, so 12 of 14 docker rows and 6 of 6 TED rows are scoring-eligible. It now reads the packet and demands the truthful statement either way, plus a refusal of any claim that a score exists
two_stale_checks_generalised.external_knowledge_markers: a module constant listing container-ecosystem words: the right check and the wrong list for any other subject. It is a parameter now, defaulting to the frozen list, so every existing caller behaves identically and this packet supplies its own

forbidden_transformations.name: REALISED_SPEND
forbidden_transformations.establishes: a stated TOTAL_VALUE at notice scope, including options and renewals

forbidden_transformations.name: MARKET_DEMAND
forbidden_transformations.establishes: that authorities published notices under one CPV class

forbidden_transformations.name: SOFTWARE_BUYER
forbidden_transformations.establishes: that a contracting authority published a notice
forbidden_transformations.is_not: a buyer, customer or prospect for a software product

forbidden_transformations.name: WILLINGNESS_TO_PAY
forbidden_transformations.establishes: an economic value stated in a published notice
forbidden_transformations.is_not: willingness to pay or a budget for software

forbidden_transformations.name: PRODUCT_MARKET_FIT
forbidden_transformations.establishes: that activity exists in a bounded set of notices
forbidden_transformations.is_not: product-market fit, a validated market or a proven need

independence_rule: independence is UNKNOWN for all six rows and there are 0 independence groups, so an output describing several independent sources is refused

human_review.why: the subject is SEMANTICALLY_COHERENT_BUT_PRODUCT_LINK_UNKNOWN and its overinterpretation risk is recorded HIGH. The gate refuses what it can name; a hypothesis that distorts the evidence without using a named phrase is exactly what it cannot name, and this is the repository's first synthesis over a procurement record. Mission 1.31 also shows the cost of the opposite mistake: a gate accepted on lexical grounds is a gate that has not read the answer
human_review.when: after the response passes every deterministic gate and before canonical persistence
